name.en: Romance scam: an online partner who needs money

how.en: Someone you meet on a dating app or social media builds a relationship with you over weeks or months, moves the chat to private messaging and always has a reason not to meet. Then there is an emergency, or their bank account is “frozen for legal reasons”, and they ask for money, often urgently and asking you to keep it secret.

text.en: A new online partner showers you with attention and moves to private messaging.
They always have a reason not to meet or video call.
They have an emergency or a frozen account and ask for money.
They ask you to keep it between the two of you.

My love, I hate to ask you this. My account is still frozen while the lawyers sort out the contract, and the hotel will throw me out tomorrow if I don’t pay. Could you send €1,200 tonight? Please don’t tell your sister, she wouldn’t understand us.

en: met on a dating app and he needs money
girlfriend i met online asked for money
keep it secret from my family online relationship
Someone you have never met in person asks for money.
Their money is “frozen” or they have a sudden emergency.
They ask you to keep it secret.
Don’t send money to someone you haven’t met in person. Talk to someone you trust.
Stop contact and keep the messages.
If you paid, call your bank and report it at your local Garda station.

sources.title: Don’t Let Romance Scammers Break Your Heart This Valentine’s Day
